diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item[(iii)] $F_{t}^{\Upsilon} = F_{t}^{\Upsilon^{\prime}}$, $F_{t, s}^{\Upsilon} = F_{t, s}^{\Upsilon^{\prime}}$ for $s \in (t, T]$, $t \in [0, T)$;

issues.failure_explanation: In \eqref{eq_recur_F} the factors F_s^{\Upsilon_i} are specific random variables, not functions of the dummy variable \theta of F_t(s,\theta), so the operator product is only meaningful as the symmetric multilinear derivative \sum F^{\Upsilon_1}_{j_1}\cdots F^{\Upsilon_l}_{j_l}\partial^l_{\theta}F_t(s,\Theta_s); that is also how it is used in the proof of Theorem thm_taylor (e.g., \eqref{eq_defGijl}, where the F^{\Upsilon_q} enter as \theta-independent coefficients of R^{n,j}). If \partial_\theta also differentiated the F_s^{\Upsilon_i} (through their state dependence), then (F^{\Upsilon_1}\cdot\partial_\theta)(F^{\Upsilon_2}\cdot\partial_\theta)F would acquire the extra term ((F^{\Upsilon_1}\cdot\partial_\theta)F^{\Upsilon_2})\cdot\partial_\theta F, the product would not commute, F_t^\Upsilon would fail to be invariant under branch permutations, and Proposition prop_Labs_equ(iii) — hence the well-definedness of F_t^{\dbr\Upsilon} in Definition def_func_Ntree and the grouping by \alpha(\Upsilon) in \eqref{eq2_Rnj_indc} — would be false. The sentence is therefore incompatible with the rest of the paper; presumably it was meant to state that the outer \partial_s^k also acts on the s-dependence of F_s^{\Upsilon_i}.

failure_location.quote: In \eqref{eq_recur_F}, the partial derivatives $\partial_{\theta}$ also act on $F_s^{\Upsilon_i}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the note, or correct it to state that the outer derivative \partial_s^k also acts on the s-dependence of the factors F_s^{\Upsilon_i}.
issues.overall_effect: Definition def_elediff, read literally with its note, is inconsistent with Proposition prop_Labs_equ(iii), with Definition def_func_Ntree, and with its own usage in the proof of Theorem thm_taylor; under the intended multilinear reading everything is consistent, so no result is lost.
issues.title: Note in Definition def_elediff makes \partial_\theta act on the coefficient vectors F_s^{\Upsilon_i}, contradicting permutation invariance
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence correction to a definition; all subsequent definitions, propositions, and proofs work unchanged under the intended reading, so no mathematical content or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: R^{n, j} = \sum_{\Upsilon \in \T_r} \frac{\alpha\br{\Upsilon} S\br{\Upsilon}}{\gamma\br{\Upsilon}} A_j^m\br{\Upsilon} \br{\Delta t_n}^{\abs{\Upsilon}} F_{t_{n, j}}^{\Upsilon} + \mO\br{\br{\Delta t}^{r+1}}, \quad \Delta t \to 0

\tilde{I}_i :=\; & \sum_{j = i+1}^m \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} \sum_{l=1}^{r-1} \sum_{\Upsilon_1 \in \widetilde{\T}_r} \sum_{\Upsilon_2 \in \widetilde{\T}_r} \cdots \sum_{\Upsilon_l \in \widetilde{\T}_r}  a_{ij} g\br{i, j, k, l, \Upsilon_1, \Upsilon_2, \cdots, \Upsilon_l}

issues.failure_explanation: In part (iv) of the proof, the sum over k, l and ordered tuples (\Upsilon_1,...,\Upsilon_l)\in\widetilde\T_r^l of B_i^m([\Upsilon_1\cdots\Upsilon_l]_k)(\Delta t_n)^{|\cdot|}F^\cdot is equated with \sum_{\Upsilon\in\widetilde\T(r)}N_P(\Upsilon)B_i^m(\Upsilon)(\Delta t_n)^{|\Upsilon|}F^\Upsilon. But LN-trees are ordered objects (Definition def_tree0; permuted trees are distinct, cf. Figure fig_equal_tree), so the bracket construction (k,l,\Upsilon_1,...,\Upsilon_l)\mapsto[\Upsilon_1\cdots\Upsilon_l]_k is a bijection onto \widetilde\T(r): each LN-tree is hit exactly once, not N_P(\Upsilon) times (N_P counts permutations that fix the ordered tuple, i.e., the product of the branch multiplicities). The inserted factor N_P(\Upsilon) is therefore spurious, and the final coefficient \frac{\alpha(\Upsilon)S(\Upsilon)}{\gamma(\Upsilon)}A_j^m(\Upsilon) in \eqref{eq2_Rnj_indc} is N_P(\Upsilon) times the correct value \frac{\alpha(\Upsilon)S(\Upsilon)}{N_P(\Upsilon)\gamma(\Upsilon)}A_j^m(\Upsilon) (per LN-tree: B_j^m(\Upsilon)=\frac{\prod_p S(\Upsilon_p)/\gamma(\Upsilon_p)}{k!\,l!}A_j^m(\Upsilon)). Concrete counterexample to the stated formula: scalar autonomous case, m=2, c_2=0, a_{12}=a\neq c_1 (allowed by Assumption assu_coeff); direct Taylor expansion of R^{n,0} — the \frac{1}{2!}(R^{n,1}\cdot\partial_\theta)^2F term of \eqref{eq_EtniDelFninj} — gives the coefficient of the order-3 elementary differential F^{[[\;]_0[\;]_0]_0} as \frac{1}{2}b_1(a-c_1)^2, whereas \eqref{eq2_Rnj_indc} states \frac{\alpha S}{\gamma}A_0^m([[\;]_0[\;]_0]_0)=b_1(a-c_1)^2, exactly twice as large (N_P=2). The same factor corrupts every tree whose root has repeated identical branches, e.g. [[\;]_0[\;]_0[\;]_0]_0, [[\;]_1[\;]_1]_0, [[\;]_1[\;]_1]_1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the factor N_P(\Upsilon) in the second line of \eqref{eq_tildeIi} (the tuple sum equals the plain tree sum by the bijection), so that \eqref{eq_Rnj_indc} holds with per-LN-tree coefficient B_j^m(\Upsilon)=\frac{\prod_p S(\Upsilon_p)/\gamma(\Upsilon_p)}{k!\,l!}A_j^m(\Upsilon), and \eqref{eq2_Rnj_indc} with per-ULN-tree coefficient \frac{\alpha(\Upsilon)S(\Upsilon)}{N_P(\Upsilon)\gamma(\Upsilon)}A_j^m(\Upsilon); no other step of the proof needs change, and all order conditions are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The error expansion \eqref{eq2_Rnj_indc} — one of the paper's two main results — is false as stated for general coefficients satisfying Assumption assu_coeff, and even for schemes satisfying all order conditions its higher-order coefficients (first at order 6, e.g. [[\;]_1[\;]_1]_1) are wrong by factors of N_P. The order conditions extracted from the expansion (\eqref{eq_ord_cond1}, C(r) in \eqref{eq_defCr}, Table tab_ordcond) are unaffected because the true and the stated coefficients vanish on exactly the same set (they differ only by the nonzero scalar N_P), so Theorem thm_consistent and the stability/convergence results thm_errest1s, thm_converge, coro_error_est survive unchanged.
issues.title: Error-expansion coefficients in Theorem thm_taylor are overstated by the symmetry factor N_P(\Upsilon) for trees with repeated identical branches
issues.why_classification: The stated expansion in a main theorem must be corrected by tree-dependent factors (up to l!), so the theorem's own claim is not preserved; but the repair is a contained formula correction requiring no new proof architecture, and every downstream guarantee (order conditions, consistency order, stability, convergence rates, numerics) is preserved verbatim, so there is no major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives the conclusion only for \Delta t_n \le \min\{1,(4m^2\bar a^2(C_{F1}+2C_{F2}\delta_c^{-1}))^{-1}\}, which is needed to guarantee 1 - 2m^2\bar a^2(C_{F1}\Delta t_n + 2C_{F2}\delta_c^{-1})\Delta t_n \ge 1/2 before dividing in \eqref{eq2_estDelFtnij}. The lemma statement asserts the same conclusion, with the stated constant \bar C_F = 4m^3\bar b^2(C_{F1}+C_{F2}\delta_c^{-1}), on the larger range \Delta t_n \le \min\{1,(4m^2\bar a^2(C_{F1}+C_{F2}\delta_c^{-1}))^{-1}\}; on the intervening interval the above factor can drop below 1/2 (as low as C_{F1}/(2(C_{F1}+C_{F2}\delta_c^{-1}))), so the stated constants are not established there.
